open_points.subject: A09 start-time refusal when credential header name collides with required header
open_points.text: "an installation whose credential header has, compared without regard to case, the name of a required header refuses to start" (A09 rule 1) + "installation ... Must not own ... reading the manifest (that is `bindings`)"
open_points.question: Which module performs this start-time cross-check across installation credentials and manifest required_headers for selected instances?
options: `service_invoker` checks only at prepare/send time (not at start)
open_points.default_guess: `service_invoker` checks at request-build time, even though that weakens the stated "refuses to start" rule

open_points.subject: Approval/resolve ended-run precondition across `runs` and `effects`
open_points.text: "whether the run has ended is checked first by `runs` ... `effects` never reads a run's status" + public `effects` capabilities include `decide_effect_approval` and `resolve_unknown_outcome`
open_points.question: Are `effects.decide_effect_approval` / `effects.resolve_unknown_outcome` valid only when called through `runs`, or must `effects` itself enforce the run-not-ended precondition?
options: Only `runs` may call them; `effects` trusts caller context
`effects` receives and trusts an explicit run-state argument
`effects` re-reads run state itself (despite the stated boundary)
open_points.default_guess: Treat them as `runs`-internal paths and rely on `runs` to enforce run-ended checks

open_points.subject: Recovery branching for operation elements (read vs non-read)
open_points.text: "No other module looks at effect classes." + `runs` owns "start-up recovery of runs left `running`" while A14 rule 5 recovery behavior differs for `read` and other operation classes
open_points.question: During `runs.recover_running_runs`, which module decides the class-dependent recovery branch for an unfinished operation element?
options: `runs` delegates each operation-element recovery step to `effects`

open_points.subject: Crash window between refusal record and run terminal state
open_points.text: State 3: "run's status and WaitingPoints ... written by `runs` in its next store call. A crash between the two leaves a run `running`, which start-up recovery advances" vs A10 rule 3: "Refusing writes one NodeExecution `refused_by_owner` ... and ends the run `refused` ... nothing further is sent."
open_points.question: How is "nothing further is sent" guaranteed if a crash occurs after `effects` writes `refused_by_owner` but before `runs` writes run status `refused`?
options: Make refusal NodeExecution + run status update one transaction
Keep two calls, but recovery must detect `refused_by_owner` first and force terminal `refused` before any send
Persist an additional terminal marker in `effects` transaction
open_points.default_guess: Recovery checks for `refused_by_owner` and finalizes `refused` before advancing any node
